rationale:
I am asking the council to ARBITRATE between two remedies, not to rubber-stamp the one I have drafted. I have a preference but low confidence in it, and the owner asked for a definitive direction rather than my instinct.

THE PROBLEM. An owner review of leopardessconsulting.co.uk found four buttons that go nowhere or lie about where they go. Diagnosis run c84940fb-6a43-47eb-86ea-eb1690b9f305 returned CONFIRMED: a CTA destination written into a section's resolved_data by resolve_internal_links at build time is re-derived by plan_sections on every later render for any field whose source is query-resolved (site_specs.*, pages.*, site_assets.*, config.*), because sourceResolver.resolve re-runs ensurePages/ensureSpecs fresh with nothing cached from the prior build. The resolver can compute the correct destination and have it overwritten. That diagnosis also CORRECTED my original claim that 'static' overrides the resolver: planSection groups static WITH renderer under one guard clause and both leave the resolver's value alone unless a fallback is declared.

Measured live against the derived CTA set: 83 url fields across 18 components are query-resolved and therefore vulnerable; 13 are immune via the renderer/static guard; 21 are source:llm (immune from this overwrite, but they are a separate fabrication defect - one of them invented the hostname leopardess.contactforsales.com, which does not exist).

THE STANDING REMEDY, AND WHY I DISTRUST IT. The platform's answer so far has been to migrate individual components' url fields to source 'renderer' one at a time, while keeping the hardcoded ctaFieldNames map in resolve_internal_links_action.go in lockstep. That is TWO hand-maintained lists that must agree for a button to be repairable, and the pair has now been amended by four separate migrations (091, 096, 097b, 098) teaching the same lesson. The map currently covers 5 of the 33 component functions that actually declare CTA url fields - roughly 15%. Everything outside it is, in the code's own words, 'detectable but not repairable'. The owner's specific concern, and mine, is that a remedy rewritten four times is a design smell rather than a maintenance cost.

WHAT I HAVE DRAFTED (option B). Derive CTA url fields from each component's input_schema - any *_url field with a sibling *_label/*_text on the same stem - in ONE shared helper, and use it at all three call sites that currently disagree: plan_sections (to stop re-resolving fields the resolver owns), resolve_internal_links (to stop consulting a hardcoded map), and applyCTARecompute (to repair beyond six components). This retires both hand-maintained lists and makes the label/url pairing exist as data, which is a precondition for ANY 'this button has no destination' check.

THE ALTERNATIVE (option A) is to keep the current architecture and simply run one more migration flipping the 83 vulnerable fields to 'renderer'. It is far less invasive, needs no Go change, and is live immediately rather than waiting on an image roll.

WHAT I GENUINELY DO NOT KNOW, AND WANT JUDGED.
1. Option B changes plan_sections - a hot path shared by every page build on every site. Is that blast radius justified to retire a migration pattern, or is it trading a known maintenance cost for an unknown correctness risk?
2. Is the sibling-label derivation rule sound as a definition of 'button destination'? It correctly excludes 32 image fields (site_assets.image/logo also end in _url), but I derived it from the current library - it may be a description of today's naming conventions rather than a rule.
3. Option A is the fifth instance of a migration that has been written four times. Does that make it the pragmatic choice or the definition of the problem?
4. If option B is right, is the staging correct? I intend to land the derivation behind a comparison log first (derive, log what WOULD change versus the map, write nothing), read one real build, then switch the write over. Deriving takes the resolver from writing ~10 fields to potentially 119.

I would rather be told option A is correct and ship it than be approved into a change I flagged as risky.

plan.summary: A button's destination can be computed correctly at build time and then silently overwritten on the next render, because plan_sections re-derives any query-resolved field (site_specs.*/pages.*/site_assets.*/config.*) from scratch and merges last. The platform has been working around this by migrating url fields to source 'renderer' one component at a time while keeping a hardcoded ctaFieldNames map in step - two hand-maintained lists, amended by four migrations, currently covering 5 of 33 CTA-bearing component functions. This plan replaces both lists with one schema-derived definition of 'CTA url field' shared by the three call sites that currently disagree, so the resolver's value is authoritative by construction rather than by per-component migration. Alternative considered and explicitly offered to the council: keep the architecture and run a fifth migration flipping the 83 vulnerable fields to 'renderer'.

edits.rationale: One definition of 'this schema field is a button destination', so plan_sections, resolve_internal_links and applyCTARecompute cannot drift apart again. Placed in datahelpers alongside links.go for the same reason links.go exists - three consumers previously each decided 'is this an internal page link' their own way and disagreed.

The exclusion case is the one that matters and is the one I got wrong in the written spec before testing it against the library: a naive '*_url' rule captures guide_image_url and logo_url. Pin it, plus determinism of ordering, plus the real shapes from tool-guide-intro and bayesian-ranking-hero-tool.

Replaces the hardcoded 6-entry map with the shared derivation, so a button-bearing component is repairable without being hand-added. STAGED: this edit only LOGS the difference between derived and mapped fields - it does not change what is written. The write switches over in a follow-up once one real build's log has been read, because derivation takes this action from writing ~10 fields to potentially 119.

THE CONTESTED EDIT - the one I want judged hardest. A CTA url field whose source is query-resolved is re-derived here on every render and overwrites the resolver's value. This makes plan_sections yield ownership of those fields instead of requiring each component to be migrated to source 'renderer' individually. It is what retires the four-times-rewritten migration; it is also a behaviour change in a hot path shared by every page build on every site.

The repair path consults the same hardcoded map, so repair scope has always been narrower than detection scope - misdirected_cta scans anchors on every component while only six could ever be repaired. Using the shared helper closes that gap in the same move rather than as a follow-up nobody schedules.

grounded_in: plan_sections_action.go:1211 — `if source == "renderer" || source == "static" || strings.HasPrefix(source, "renderer.") || strings.HasPrefix(source, "static.") { if fallback != nil { resolvedData[fieldName] = fallback }; continue }`

resolve_internal_links_action.go:83-86 — `The misdirected_cta discovery check scans anchors on EVERY component, so a button-bearing component missing from this set is detectable but not repairable — its findings can only escalate to human review.`

resolve_internal_links_action.go:86-90 — `A component added here must ALSO have its url fields' schema source flipped to "renderer" (migrations 091, 098): a site_specs.*/pages.*/static source is re-resolved into resolved_data on every render and merges last, so no recompute or content edit can win against it.`

Diagnosis c84940fb conclusion — `The fields that DO get freshly re-queried on every plan_sections call (and so can overwrite a value resolve_internal_links previously wrote into resolved_data) are exactly those whose source string reaches sourceResolver.resolve() — site_specs.*, pages.*, site_assets.*, or config.* — not 'static'.`

Diagnosis c84940fb, live schema evidence — `"cta_url": {"type": "url", "source": "pages.contact", "fallback": "/contact.html", "required": false, "on_missing": "use_fallback"}` on header-bold-gradient/site-header

Measured against the live library 2026-07-19: derived CTA url fields = 119 across 33 component functions; ctaFieldNames covers 5 of those 33; by source, 83 are query-resolved (vulnerable), 13 renderer/static (immune), 21 llm; a naive '*_url' rule without the sibling-label test additionally captures 32 site_assets.image/logo fields.

Measured against the live library 2026-07-19: 75 of 89 URL-bound CTA anchors in active component templates are ungated (no enclosing {{if .x_url}}), so an empty value renders href="" rather than rendering no button — the stated LNK-005 invariant is violated by ~84% of them.
plan.risks:
1. The plan_sections edit is in a hot path shared by every page build on every site; a wrong field set there suppresses legitimate source resolution. Mitigated by the sibling-label test (verified to exclude all 32 image/logo url fields) and by honouring declared fallbacks, but a reviewer should check the case of a component that legitimately wants its CTA url from site_specs as deliberate site-level config — I believe that case IS the bug (it is what locked 143 of 144 buttons to /contact.html) but I may be wrong.
2. Deriving takes resolve_internal_links from ~10 fields to potentially 119. Staged as observe-only in this round precisely so the delta is read before it is trusted; a reviewer should confirm the staging is real and not decorative.
3. The derivation rule may describe today's naming conventions rather than a durable contract. If a component names a destination field without a matching label, it silently drops out of both detection and repair — the same failure mode as the map, moved.
4. applyCTARecompute widens the field set it can repair; the keep-rule is deliberately unchanged so that widening what is REPAIRABLE does not widen what is OVERWRITTEN. Worth checking I have not accidentally done both.
5. Go changes are inert until an image is rebuilt and rolled, so this cannot be verified in prod on the same day it lands; the migration alternative (option A) is live immediately. That asymmetry is a real argument for option A and I have not weighted it confidently.
